findings.title: Require completed owner effects before committing first-use rows
findings.description: lock_daily_head(create_first=True) and lock_execution(create_first=True) now execute real INSERTs directly on RepositoryTransaction. Their first_execution_head/first_execution_session completion checks exist only in RestrictedSqlSession.validate_completion, which runs only if the callback invokes idempotent_outcome. RepositoryTransaction.finish checks registry, subject and exact artifacts but never checks whether a newly inserted first-use row completed its owner outcome. Thus an existing internal execute_command StartSession callback can acquire the registry lease, validate its artifact identities and authenticated TEST ingress, call lock_execution on an absent exact session with create_first=True, and return. finish accepts this and the outer transaction commits a bare APP_STARTED/READY revision-zero S44 without START S45, execution-basis event, receipt, event or outbox. CommitBundle has the equivalent bare S38 path after its intent/fence/day guards. This introduces a mutation that can escape the mandatory completion boundary even though the typed service itself currently calls idempotent_outcome.
findings.requirement: KL-019 Existing owner reuse and bounded missing capabilities requires owner mutation/completion checks proving the exact newly inserted row and required complete effects; all first-use effects must be atomic. Frozen Protocol §2.1 and §8, DB §5 T6/T7, S38 and S44/S45 require the owner effects and bookkeeping together. The existing read-only owner/query callback use does not justify committing these newly added writes without completion.

Independent pure control-flow probe used a fake cursor and symbolic already-established owner guard state, called real RepositoryTransaction.lock_execution(create_first=True) then finish, and observed finish accepting its sole S44 INSERT without idempotent_outcome. No PostgreSQL or lifecycle operations were performed by the reviewer.
findings.required_change: Make the existing owner finish boundary reject every newly created S38/S44 unless the matching owner outcome completed successfully with its exact required effects. Keep read-only owner operations valid when they created no row. Add real PostgreSQL negative owner callbacks that return immediately after each first-use creation, asserting denial and exact baseline preservation; retain positive first-use and rollback evidence and rerun all exact packet checks on the repaired implementation.

findings.title: Recover historical receipt when authority changes after a missing preflight
findings.description: All three execution operations call _registry before execution_historical_outcome. _registry invokes existing guards that obtain S51/S01 and enforce live current Manifest/epoch, issuance time and/or artifact revocation eligibility before returning. Consider retry R whose replay_outcome preflight obtains S01 before the original O starts and finds no receipt, then releases S01. O commits the same request while R is delayed outside coordination; a control/epoch change, expiry or registry revoke then occurs before R enters the owner. R fails the live registry guard before its under-S01 historical lookup despite the now-durable identical receipt. There is no rollback-and-read-only-replay recovery. This is distinct from a retry whose receipt already existed when replay_outcome obtained S01: that ordinary preflight path correctly returns the historical outcome and is covered by the existing tests. The new under-S01 lookup does not close the former race when current authority has been lost.
findings.requirement: Frozen DB §3 requires same-key same-payload historical replay and distinguishes it from current authorization; repository_transactions.md states ACK-loss replay is available without reacquiring registry/live guards. KL-019 execution_ack_loss_replay_dc requires historical START after authority loss/expiry/revocation to remain available, replayed=true and executable=false, with no remutation.

src/kineticloop/persistence/transactions.py:4992 replay_outcome locks S01 then S02; a missing receipt releases those locks before the later execution owner transaction

tests/db/test_protocol_execution.py:1260 same-key contention pauses the winner after acquiring S01; the loser therefore blocks inside its replay_outcome preflight and discovers the committed receipt there. It does not establish the missing-preflight then authority-loss interleaving.
findings.required_change: Preserve the existing registry algorithms and lock order, while ensuring an identical successful receipt can still be returned after an owner guard failure if it was committed after missing preflight; a bounded read-only replay after owner transaction rollback is one possible approach. Never grant a current action from that recovery and keep changed-payload conflicts distinct. Add bounded real PostgreSQL interleavings that pause the retry after a genuine missing preflight, commit the original, apply the existing control/revocation owner or trusted expiry condition, then resume the retry and assert exact historical IDs, executable=false and no persisted changes. Cover publication/commit historical identity where applicable as well as START.
